correctness.rationale: For positive parameters the product G is strictly Hurwitz-stable; the full Hermite–Biehler theorem supplies simple negative interlaced P and Q zeros with rightmost P. The map t -> (1-t)^(-1) preserves their order, giving J <=st K <=st J+1. Common-quantile coupling then forces K-J in {0,1}; boundary points follow by finite-support continuity with positive conditioning masses. The cost lower bound is the fixed lattice separation. Darroch strict mode proximity and half-integer spacing yield sharp 3/2, attained by an exact two-factor example. The 115,171 exact rational exhaustive grid cases stress-tested all CDF and modal bounds but are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: A full distribution-level identity for every Wasserstein exponent, uniform over sample sizes and heterogeneous trinomial parameters, is a natural and nontrivial strengthening of separate log-concavity and mean proximity. The sharp 3/2 modal boundary resolves the explicit 5/2 gap left in the motivating parity-structure paper; both optimality claims have exact witnesses. The coupling supplies an explicit quantile algorithm relevant to score parity comparisons.
